reviews.author: BOBBEY AXELORD
reviews.text:
1. Bun Bossao

2. Rice noodles + salty

3. Premium rice noodles

​

I visited Ben Thanh Villa Konkuk University branch a total of 3 times.  It's not a great restaurant, but I thought it would be a good place to eat for the day. The first and second visits were okay, but the premium rice noodles I ordered on my third visit today were so delicious that I couldn't agree more. The description says it's [high-quality rice noodles made with brisket rice noodles and added beef sauce], but the amount of meat was absolutely insufficient and the noodles were clumped together in the corners. I added a lot of bean sprouts, but I couldn't find any lumps of noodles in the corners, so I thought there were no noodles. The most critical problem was that the soup was almost tasteless. It was so close to soup that I couldn't even taste it. In my subjective judgment, it even tasted like water. These are premium rice noodles? I absolutely do not agree.

​

You can see on my blog that many people are looking for Seongsu-Gondae pho restaurants. I decided that Ben Thanh Villa Konkuk University branch was the least delicious place, so I deleted it from the pho list. I won't be visiting again.

I also ordered beef and egg porridge, and the porridge boiled in shabu-shabu broth was really filling and delicious.

It's perfect for eating alone as it's an induction cooker for one person, and the bear-shaped ice (broth) is really cute!

The price was cheap, around 10,000 won, and it was good value for money, so I was convinced.

I 100% intend to go again if I pass by Konkuk University. Friendly and delicious, highly recommended!

reviews.text: After going to an auto repair shop, I was looking for the closest restaurant and ended up there by chance. Is there an Italian restaurant like this in a place that is so ridiculously hard to find? I wasn't expecting much and thought I would just grab a meal, but I was surprised when they asked me if I had made a reservation because there was no place to sit! Wow, I never thought a place like this would be bustling with people! I had a hunch. You can't open a restaurant here unless the food is truly excellent! As expected, it was delicious. The panini salad was also excellent value for money at 7,000 won, and the tomato cream pasta had a really rich flavor in the sauce. On the other hand, compared to the other two, the risotto is relatively so-so. Still, it was all delicious. I guess I was lucky to find this restaurant by chance!

It is a Hong Kong/Taiwanese dessert shop located on the main street near the entrance to Konkuk University, which is crowded with lamb skewer restaurants and Chinese grocery stores. There is another store near Kyunghee University and there was once a branch in Hongdae, but it is now closed.

Although the chain is not expanding in earnest, it strangely gives the impression of being the ‘Haidi Lao of the dessert world.’ All the employees were Chinese and most of the customers were Chinese, so I thought I was in China.

The menu features Hong Kong-style desserts such as pudding and Taiwanese desserts such as milk tea-based shaved ice. In addition, they also sell crepe-shaped towel cakes and other trendy Chinese desserts.

Since I wanted to eat mango sago, I ordered Yangzhi Ganlu, which is based on mango sago. It is still expensive compared to China, but considering it is Korea, the price is reasonable and the quality is quite good.

Yangzhi Ganlu is a dessert made by adding grapefruit and pomelo pulp to mango sago and finishing it with coconut milk. If the basic mango sago is sweet, this is much sour and refreshing thanks to the acidity, and the taste is more complex.

The mango puree has a slurpable texture, and the sago pearls embedded in it add a chewy texture. There was also a large mango in it, and although it was frozen, the amount was not overwhelming and the sweetness was clearly delivered.

The menu is one that can be found at Chinese dessert restaurants in Taiwan or Southeast Asia, so it brings back memories of a fun trip. I ordered a Chinese dessert called melted shaved ice, which is often found in Taiwan and other parts of Southeast Asia, and it tasted just right. It's not a strong sweet taste, but it's mildly sweet and not overpowering. In some ways, it can be said to be bland, but it's easy to eat and has a variety of toppings, so it's a fun dessert to try.
The towel cake is similarly not sweet and has a less pungent taste than other places.
The overall taste is less spicy, so some people may not like it, but it is a place that has the pleasure of stimulating nostalgia for travel.

reviews.author: DASIT
reviews.text:
Small bakery located near Hwayang Jeil Market near Konkuk University Station

Although this place, run by young people, is not large in scale, it offers a variety of breads, including garlic bread, and is a bakery that many people visit simply because of its taste.

A unique feature of this place is that the rankings of the five most popular menu items are displayed directly in the menu names of the breads on display, so if first-time visitors have difficulty choosing a product when purchasing a product, they refer to it and select a product that suits their tastes and characteristics without much failure.

The only thing that is unfortunate is that although the cakes here are delicious, they do not have a variety of cakes except for the year-end and Christmas seasons, and you have to order in advance before purchasing some of the items they make. However, it is understandable as it is a small store.

All of the menu items on offer are delicious, but I personally liked the pollack roe baguette, garlic bread, and salt bread.

When visiting by car, it is located in a narrow alley, so it is possible to park for a while in front of the store, but it is difficult to find ample parking, so it is convenient to use public or private parking lots nearby.

reviews.author: BH Park
reviews.text:
It is located near the entrance of the first basement level of Lotte Department Store, so it is easy to find. The main store is located in Seongbuk-gu, Seoul and is said to have opened in 1968. In other words, it seems to be a very famous bakery from the past and is already famous among people of various ages. As soon as I saw my mom's name, I recognized it right away. Anyway, the branch located at Lotte Department Store's Konkuk University branch is directly managed by the main branch, and the bread is said to taste better than non-directly managed stores.

Personally, looking at the salt bread alone, I thought it was a bit more delicious here than Iseongdang and Auerbake on the first basement level of Jamsil Lotte.
